name: Trace
tagline: Daily tech-news briefings that group related coverage, summarize context, and link the sources

pricing.notes: The public site describes the core briefing as free; no public paid price was found.

verdictSummary: A personal multi-source briefing can be built from RSS feeds and an LLM, but it takes ongoing source curation, deduplication, clustering, and careful attribution to stay useful. Trace's value is the maintained daily pipeline and readable editorial synthesis rather than an impossible feature set.
coreLoopDIY: Poll a fixed set of tech RSS feeds, cluster near-duplicate stories, summarize each topic with linked sources, and render one daily briefing.
moatNotes: RSS and LLM summaries are accessible; dependable aggregation is continuing operational work.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay when the briefing is already clean every morning: sources are curated, duplicate coverage is grouped, summaries preserve context, and every claim stays easy to trace back to reporting.

priorArt.name: FreshRSS
priorArt.desc: Mature self-hosted RSS aggregator and reader.

notes: The replacement intentionally stays personal and source-linked instead of claiming a universal news index.
prompt:
Build a personal daily tech-news briefing in an empty repository.

Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Prisma, rss-parser, and a Node cron worker.
The core loop is: poll a fixed RSS source list, normalize and deduplicate items,
cluster related stories, summarize each cluster, and render one daily briefing.
Keep feeds in a versioned sources.json with name, URL, and category.
Use an LLM API key from .env only after deterministic title, URL, and time clustering.
Store original URLs, source names, publication dates, cluster membership, and summaries.
Show every source link beside the summary; distinguish one-source stories from multi-source topics.
Provide a daily archive, source filters, a refresh command, and visible stale or failed-feed states.
Rate-limit requests, use conditional HTTP fetches, and retain raw feed metadata for debugging.
Use a local-only database and export the briefing data as JSON.
Write a README with setup, source-copyright limits, data location, and model cost notes.
Do not add accounts, paywall bypassing, publisher scraping, personalized recommendation training, telemetry, or claims of comprehensive coverage.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
